task: Add a Koala-managed Codex adapter manifest and harden the Codex CLI wrapper without creating fake Codex hooks/settings runtime files.
outcome: After a user runs koala init, they see .Codex/koala.json describing adapterOwner=koala, recommendedEntrypoint=bin/koala-codex.js or KOALA_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex koala, activitySource=codex, and excludedRuntimeAssets=[.Codex/hooks,.Codex/settings.json]. .Codex/README.md tells them Codex gets a Koala adapter, not Claude-style hooks/settings.
facts: bin/koala-codex.js already sets KOALA_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex and derives KOALA_ACTIVITY_SESSION from Codex/OpenAI/terminal session environment variables.
Codex does not consume .Codex/hooks or .Codex/settings.json as a runtime convention in this project.
Koala init already writes .Codex/README.md and mirrors .claude/agents prompts into .Codex/agents.
constraints: The adapter manifest must be explicit that it is Koala-managed, not Codex runtime-owned.
Tests must prove the wrapper tags source=codex and init emits the adapter manifest.
